$comment: What lab/servicenow/apply.py builds on the ServiceNow PDI. Names, not sys_ids: apply.py finds each record by name and creates or updates it, so a re-run changes only what differs.
Access packages are named, not pinned by id: apply.py resolves each one live through Microsoft Graph as the lab operator and fails if a name matches zero or two packages.
No secrets here. The repo is public.

category.title: Access & accounts
category.description: Ask for access to a hospital app, report a leaver, or get help signing in.

iamQueue.name: IAM Operations
iamQueue.description: Identity and access management: access requests that need a person, sign-in and MFA problems, leaver access removal. Changes in Entra carry the ticket number.
iamQueue.membersNote: ServiceNow accounts come from Entra provisioning (App-ServiceNow-Users); queue membership and the itil role are ServiceNow's own, set here.

requestItem.name: Request app access
requestItem.short_description: Ask for access to a clinical app. Your manager approves; access is granted in Microsoft Entra ID automatically and ends on the date you choose.
requestItem.description:
Use this when your job needs an app your role does not give you on day one, for example ICU float cover.

What happens next:

  1. Your manager gets an approval.
  2. When they approve, ServiceNow asks Microsoft Entra ID to grant the access. You usually have it within a few minutes.
  3. Access ends by itself on the end date (180 days at most).

No patient data is entered here.

leaverItem.name: Report a leaver: remove app access
leaverItem.short_description: For managers: someone is leaving. HR disables the account; this removes the extra app access they asked for.

accessRequestList.title: Access requests (IAM)
accessRequestList.note: One list, grouped by state (the group headers carry the counts) with Duration = opened to closed (time to fulfil). A list, not a sys_report chart: on dev459905 the report_view field ACLs refused the chart to an itil user (seen 2026-11-07), while lists follow the ordinary read ACLs the queue already uses.
